facts.raw_span: intermittent palpitations for 2 days
no history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
no past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
respiratory rate was 14 bpm
Cardiovascular system examination results were unremarkable
Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
atypical left bundle branch morphology (QS in leads V1-V5 with transition in V6)
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Global hypokinesia of right ventricle, dilated RV, ballooned out RVOT measuring 35 mm
Grossly dilated RV, high RV end diastolic volume of 219.9 mL, RVOT diameter of 31 mm, RV ejection fraction of 19.3%
Postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall, RVOT apical wall, RV aspect of septum, and in basal inferior, midcavity inferior, and inferoseptal myocardium of left ventricle

concepts.why: The patient's ECG and cardiac MRI findings, including wide complex tachycardia and grossly dilated RV, are consistent with ARVC.
The patient's ECG findings, including wide complex tachycardia and atypical left bundle branch morphology, are consistent with VT.
The patient's echocardiography and cardiac MRI findings, including dilated RVOT, are consistent with RVOT dilation.
The patient's echocardiography and cardiac MRI findings, including global hypokinesia of right ventricle, are consistent with RV dysfunction.
The patient's cardiac MRI findings, including postcontrast hyperenhancement, are consistent with cardiac sarcoidosis.
The patient's ECG findings, including wide complex tachycardia, are consistent with idiopathic VT.
The patient's echocardiography and cardiac MRI findings, including dilated RV, are consistent with right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
The patient's ECG findings, including wide complex tachycardia, may be related to an underlying electrolyte imbalance.

rationales.F01: Palpitations are a common symptom of various cardiac conditions, including arrhythmias and cardiomyopathies.
rationales.F07: Wide complex tachycardia is a characteristic feature of ventricular tachycardia and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F08: Atypical left bundle branch morphology is often seen in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F09: Prolonged QRS duration without AV dissociation is consistent with ventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F10: Global hypokinesia and dilation of the right ventricle are characteristic features of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F11: Grossly dilated right ventricle and reduced ejection fraction are indicative of right ventricular dysfunction.
rationales.F12: Postcontrast hyperenhancement along the right ventricular free wall and septum is consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and cardiac sarcoidosis.
